Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Searched for statutory or regulatory data-breach notification requirements in Togo (including cybersecurity or data protection requirements applicable to payment/financial service providers); no clear mandatory breach-notification obligation found in accessible sources.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single light-check search surfaced a clearly authoritative, directly on-point source, so the row was moved from the fast path to the full path. Fetched and read BCEAO Instruction N°001-03-2021 (regional central bank regulation binding on Togo as a UEMOA/BCEAO member state), which at Article 10 obliges payment institutions, payment instrument issuers and financial market infrastructure managers ('assujettis') to notify the BCEAO within 24 hours of any incident causing a service interruption of more than two hours, followed by a detailed report within three calendar days, with financial penalties and possible suspension of authorisation for non-compliance. This is a mandatory, time-bound incident/breach notification obligation to the sector regulator, so the score is raised from 0 (Unknown, no source cited) to 3 (Mandatory). Cross-checked against DataGuidance's Togo jurisdiction profile, which confirms Togo's general Data Protection Act (Law No. 2019-014) does not itself contain data breach notification provisions, so the enforceable obligation for payment providers rests on the regional BCEAO instrument rather than national data protection law.
revised_comments: Togo, as a UEMOA member state, is subject to BCEAO Instruction N°001-03-2021 on the oversight of financial market infrastructures and payment instruments/services. Article 10 requires payment service providers, payment instrument issuers and financial market infrastructure managers to notify the BCEAO of any incident causing a service interruption exceeding two hours within 24 hours of its occurrence, followed by a detailed report within three calendar days; non-compliance carries financial penalties and, ultimately, suspension or withdrawal of authorisation. Togo's national Data Protection Act (Law No. 2019-014) does not itself impose a data breach notification duty, so the operative mandatory-notification regime applicable to payment providers derives from this regional central bank regulation.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: Searched for publicly available PI‑SPI/PI‑PSI (or other Togo retail payment system) scheme rulebooks/operating rules/specifications published for the public; no official scheme rulebook or rules portal located in accessible sources.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-check search surfaced the BCEAO's official public portal for PI-SPI (Togo's instant payment system, operated regionally by the BCEAO), moving this row to the full path. The portal's public FAQ (pispi.bceao.int/foire-aux-questions) sets out core scheme rules without registration: eligible participant/account types, the four client categories (P/C/B/G), the rule distinguishing a free 'transfer' from a chargeable 'payment' (a cap of 30 transfers per calendar month to a type-P client), and free peer-to-peer transfers. This is genuine public disclosure of some scheme rules, so the score is raised from 0 to 2 (Partial). It falls short of confirmed evidence of a complete, formally published rulebook covering participation criteria, pricing structure, technical and security standards for participants, so it is not scored 3 (Fully Public) and is flagged for human review to check whether a fuller technical rulebook exists.
revised_comments: Togo's instant payment functionality is delivered through the BCEAO's regional PI-SPI platform, launched across the eight UEMOA member states on 30 September 2025. The BCEAO publishes a public FAQ (pispi.bceao.int) explaining core scheme rules, including client categories, the free peer-to-peer transfer facility, and the threshold (30 transactions per calendar month) distinguishing a 'transfer' from a chargeable 'payment'. This provides a degree of public transparency over the scheme's rules, though it is not confirmed whether a complete technical rulebook covering participant obligations, pricing and security standards is separately published.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: World Bank case study describes NOVISSI program management including grievance mechanisms and daily reconciliation, but did not provide explicit evidence of independent/private/public audits of national payment systems or PI‑SPI operator audits in sources reviewed.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-check search surfaced IFAC's Togo country profile, an authoritative source on the national audit framework, moving this row to the full path. IFAC confirms Togo has no independent public audit-oversight authority; statutory audits are governed by the regional OHADA accounting framework (SYSCOHADA/AUDCIF) and supervised by ONECCA-Togo under Ministry of Economy and Finance oversight, with no separate independent body publishing audit findings. A licensed local firm (AUDITCOM-TOGO) confirms that BCEAO regulation makes external audit of decentralised financial systems (microfinance institutions, payment establishments) mandatory as part of prudential compliance. Together this supports code 2 (Private Audits: audits are conducted under regulatory requirement, but results are not made public), raised from 0.
revised_comments: External audits of financial and payment institutions operating in Togo are mandated under BCEAO/UMOA prudential regulation and the OHADA accounting framework (SYSCOHADA/AUDCIF), and licensed firms conduct statutory audits of decentralised financial systems, including payment and microfinance institutions, for regulatory-compliance purposes. Togo has no independent public audit-oversight authority, however, and audit results are not published; oversight is exercised through the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the professional body ONECCA-Togo rather than through public disclosure of findings.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Searched for quantified share of government payments digitized in Togo (e.g., % of treasury flows, salaries, social transfers) but did not find an official percentage measure in accessible sources; found only qualitative references to digitization initiatives.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-check search surfaced substantial World Bank documentation on Togo's Novissi G2P programme, moving this row to the full path. Evidence found: Novissi, Togo's COVID-19 emergency cash-transfer programme, was delivered fully digitally end-to-end via mobile money (using electoral-register and telecom data in lieu of a social registry), created 170,278 new mobile money accounts (a 7% rise in national mobile money penetration) by January 2021, and is cited by the World Bank as an exemplar of rapid, fully digital G2P delivery, later feeding into a Safety Nets and Basic Services Project. However, none of the sources reviewed give an aggregate percentage of ALL government payments (including public-sector salaries and pensions, not just the one flagship social-transfer programme) made digitally, which is what this variable requires. Assigning a specific percentage band (the variable's scale) from programme-level qualitative evidence alone would be a guess rather than a grounded score, so this is flagged for human review rather than upgraded.
revised_comments: Togo's most prominent government-to-person digitisation is the Novissi emergency cash-transfer programme, delivered end-to-end digitally via mobile money using data cross-referenced from the electoral register and telecommunications records in the absence of a formal social registry. The programme created 170,278 new mobile money accounts (a 7% increase in national mobile money penetration) by January 2021 and has been cited by the World Bank as an exemplar of rapid, fully digital G2P delivery, later informing a broader Safety Nets and Basic Services Project. Comprehensive public data on the proportion of all government payments, including public-sector salaries and pensions, made through the instant payment system rather than cash or cheque is not available.
